claims.claim: newMux only registers GET /{$}; there is no /hello route today.

scenario.then: the response is 200 with body "hello, world"
the response is 405, since only GET is registered for the route

overview.objective: Add a greet package with a fixed hello message, delivered as three small build tasks, so a later ticket can wire it into the HTTP server.
overview.context: cmd/zing/main.go builds the HTTP server and its routes in newMux; this ticket delivers the greeting itself as a standalone package and a fixture marker file, ahead of the route that will call it.
overview.problem: Nothing today provides a fixed greeting a route handler could call, so there is no minimal, tested unit to build the eventual /hello route on top of.

goals.goal: A greet package exposes a Greet function that returns the fixed text "hello, world"
The build produces one signed commit per task, in order

nongoals.nongoal: Accepting a name parameter or personalizing the greeting is out of scope; this delivers a fixed-text helper, not a templated one
Wiring the greet package into newMux is a later ticket; this one stops at the package and its test

design.demo: Once task 1 lands, the project's own test command finds hello.txt on disk, the smallest slice that shows the build loop writing a real file through to a signed commit.
design.shape: Three files, each its own task and its own commit: hello.txt, a fixture marker file the project's test command checks for; greet.go, a package-level Greet function returning the fixed text; and greet_test.go, the test that pins its return value.

files.file: a fixture marker file task 1 writes so the project's test command has something to find
the greet package and its Greet function, task 2

tests.test: Greet() returns the fixed text "hello, world"

tasks.task: Add the greeting file hello.txt so the project's test command, `test -f hello.txt`, has something to find.
Add the greet package with a Greet function that returns the fixed text "hello, world".
Add greet_test.go, covering Greet's fixed return value.

alternatives.alternative: Deliver all three files in one task: rejected, since the build loop commits one task at a time, and this plan exists to exercise that loop across more than a single task.

risks.risk: None of these files is wired into the running server yet; a later ticket connects Greet to the /hello route.

reply.question: Q1
reply.decision: Use the recommended greeting text: hello, world.
